evidence: Clear module-based organization with 4 top-level packages (mps_youtube, doc, docs, .github) and deep nesting (max_directory_depth=3) indicating logical grouping by responsibility
High average fan-out (5.0) suggests modules heavily depend on internal components rather than external services, typical of monoliths
Domain-driven module structure: commands/, players/, listview/, content/, playlist/, config, util, screen, mpris, etc., each with cohesive responsibilities
Central shared state via global module g.py and shared data structures (Content, Playlist, Video classes)
No evidence of service boundaries, inter-service communication, or deployment isolation—everything runs in one process
Test suite is co-located with source (mps_youtube/test/), common in monolithic architectures
Single entry point (main.py) orchestrating the application flow
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., many modules import g, c, config directly) may hinder maintainability and testing
Global state in g.py and c.py increases risk of side effects and makes concurrent execution unsafe
High fan-out indicates potential for circular dependencies and reduced modularity over time
